Job Description:
About Shiftbase

We build workforce software that helps people get work done. More than 10,000 companies use our platform every month to plan shifts and track time, with less admin in the way.

We work from our Zoetermeer office with over 80 people and we grow every year. The culture is open and informal. You can push back on an idea regardless of title, and we change how we work when someone makes the case in retro.

About The Role

You build frontend features that customers use the day you release them. You sit in a product team with backend, QA, design and product, and you take a feature from a rough product idea to a screen a planner can use without a manual.

Your time is a balance between working on features, bugs and resolving technical debt.

Claude Code is how our engineers write software. Everyone here uses it daily, and whole features now go out with an agent doing most of the coding. You still own what you merge, so you read the diff, you know why it works, and you can defend it in review. The interesting part of the job is deciding what to hand to an agent, what to write yourself, and what context the agent needs to get it right the first time.

You ask what a planner is trying to do before you read what the ticket says. You automate the parts of your own process that don't need a human.

Year one, in order

First, ship. Deliver features in scheduling and time tracking. Start small, then take one full feature from the product conversation through to release.

Then, own an area. Pick up a product surface end to end and become the person the team asks about it, including what it should do next. That covers how AI fits your area, which patterns you document for the agent and which calls you keep for yourself.

Along the way, make what you build safe to change. Restructure and test the paths you build on while you build on them. Extend test coverage where it's lacking. We move fast and keep quality up by automating what a human doesn't need to do, including the checks that catch what an agent got wrong.

What You'll Do

Design and build frontend features starting from rough product ideas
Deliver features with Claude Code, from the prompt through to the pull request, and review the output as closely as a colleague's
Write the patterns, conventions and project context our agents work from, so generated frontend code lands in the right shape
Turn tangled domain rules into screens people can use without a manual
Fix bugs in your own features and in code you've never seen
Improve the code you touch while you touch it, so the next feature in that area costs less
Write and maintain automated tests in Jest and Playwright
Ship in short cycles with your product team
Pair, review, and teach what you know


How We Work

Frontend in Angular, backend in PHP, a web app and a mobile app in React Native. Tests in Jest and Playwright. We develop AI-assisted with Claude Code as the primary tool, and a growing share of our code starts there. Human review and engineers owning what they ship keep it safe. We ship in short cycles in product teams with mixed specialisations. We pair often, with each other and with an agent open. Every quarter you get time to build and ship one of your own ideas, and we run hackathons.

Must-haves

3+ years of professional experience with an SPA framework, Angular preferred. Depth in React or Vue works if you can show you'll carry it over.

You ship. You've delivered features to real users at a steady pace, and you can tell us what you cut to get them out.

You've shipped production code with an AI agent. Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or similar. Tell us where you let it run, where you took the keyboard back, and what you changed about your own workflow after a month of it.

You automate your tests. Jest and Playwright, or equivalents, and you have an opinion about what deserves a test.

You simplify. Hand you a tangled domain problem and you produce a screen that hides the tangle.

You explain your choices. In review, in a design discussion, and to a product manager who doesn't read code.

You work as a peer. You pair, you review, and you make the people around you better without needing a title to be heard.

Nice-to-haves

Claude Code in particular, or agent setups you've tuned for a team rather than yourself
TypeScript at depth
Storybook or component library ownership
React
TDD
PHP, or enough backend to reason about the API you're consuming
Familiarity with a complex, regulated domain (ours covers scheduling, time tracking, leave, and labour law across countries)


This might be your dream job if…

✅ You want your work in front of customers within days

✅ You'd rather own a feature end to end than take a finished spec

✅ You want a say in how a team writes frontend code with agents while the answer is still open

✅ You improve the code you touch without being asked, and you stop before it turns into a six-week rewrite

✅ You like a domain that takes months to learn

This probably isn't your dream job if…

⛔️ You want the technical approach decided before the ticket reaches you

⛔️ You want a job where AI stays out of your editor

⛔️ You'd merge agent output you can't explain in review

⛔️ You'd stop shipping to finish a refactor

⛔️ You prefer pixel work and would rather leave tests and architecture to someone else

⛔️ You'd rather work alone than pair and review

32 or 40 hours workweek 
Hybrid, from home or the Zoetermeer office
25 vacation days based on a 40-hour contract
Pension plan
NS business card or travel expenses reimbursed. 
Training budget for personal development

Job Description:
About Us
Data Oriented Defence Operations (DODO OÜ) is a cutting-edge Cybersecurity boutique based in Tallinn, Estonia. We operate at the forefront of the Deep Tech industry, and yes, it's time to say it openly: we proudly emerged from the NATO ecosystem. We specialize in advanced Defence and Security solutions, pushing the boundaries of what is possible in autonomous offensive security.
The Role
We are looking for a Penetration Tester / Red Teamer to join us as the offensive-security backbone of ARES, our autonomous red-teaming platform powered by Agentic AI.
This is not a classic pentest role. Your job is to be the human red teamer that ARES has to measure up to. You will build the environments ARES attacks, run engagements against those same targets yourself, and compare what you found against what the AI found — then feed that gap back to the engineering team as concrete product improvements. In practice you are equal parts operator and QA: you break things, and you make the machine better at breaking things.
This is a part-time position of approximately 20 hours per week, fully remote, with flexible scheduling — designed to be compatible with a Master's program or other ongoing commitments.
Eligibility
Given the nature of our work in the Defence and Security sector, this role requires EU/EEA citizenship and residency in Europe. We appreciate the interest of candidates outside these criteria, but unfortunately we cannot move forward with those applications at this stage.
Compensation & Company Stage — Please Read Carefully
We want to be completely transparent about where DODO stands today, so you can make an informed decision.
We are pre-funding and currently working to close our first investment round. Concretely:
The role begins with a 4-month trial period, which is unpaid. During this period we are not in a position to provide either salary or equity.
If the funding round closes, the role converts to a paid position with stock options, on terms set out in the Memorandum of Understanding we sign at the outset.
If the round does not close, we will not be able to offer either. We would rather say this openly now than have you discover it in four months.
We understand this is a significant ask, and it will not be the right fit for everyone — that's entirely reasonable. The ~20h/week structure is intended to make it workable alongside studies or other work. If it's not your situation right now, we genuinely understand, and we'd welcome hearing from you again once we're funded.
What You Will Do
Target & Range Engineering: Design and build deliberately vulnerable environments — web applications, APIs, cloud misconfigurations, Active Directory labs, container escapes — that serve as ARES' training and testing ground.
Adversarial QA: Manually attack those same targets and benchmark your results against ARES' autonomous runs. Where the AI missed a path, stalled, or produced a false positive, you document why.
Attack Path Definition: Translate real-world TTPs (mapped to MITRE ATT&CK) into scenarios and success criteria the platform can be evaluated against.
Product Feedback Loop: Work directly with the Agentic AI team to turn operational findings into concrete backlog items — better tooling, better reasoning, better reporting.
Reporting & Validation: Assess the quality of ARES' output — are the findings accurate, reproducible, and written the way a client would need to read them?
Automation: Script target deployment and test scenarios (Python, Bash, Docker) so environments can be spun up repeatably during QA and UAT cycles.
Cross-functional Bridging: Act as the operational security voice inside an AI engineering team.
What We Are Looking For
Hands-on offensive security experience — internships, professional engagements, CTFs, bug bounty, or a serious home lab. You can walk us through an attack chain you executed end to end.
Web and network penetration testing fundamentals: OWASP Top 10, authentication and authorization flaws, injection, SSRF, privilege escalation, lateral movement.
Practical command of the standard toolkit: Burp Suite, Nmap, Metasploit, Impacket, BloodHound, or equivalents — and an understanding of what they do under the hood.
Scripting ability in Python and Bash — enough to automate a target build, not just run other people's tools.
Comfort with Linux, containers, and cloud environments (Docker, and at least one major cloud provider).
Familiarity with MITRE ATT&CK and structured thinking about adversary behavior.
Clear written communication — findings that another engineer can act on.
Bachelor's or Master's degree (enrolled or completed) in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a closely related field — or equivalent demonstrated experience.
Ability to work autonomously on goal-oriented tasks in a fully remote environment, managing your own ~20h/week schedule.
Nice to Have
Offensive security certifications (OSCP, PNPT, CRTO, eJPT, or similar) — or actively working toward one.
Active Directory attack experience and red team operational tradecraft (C2 frameworks, evasion).
Experience building CTF challenges, vulnerable labs, or cyber range environments.
Familiarity with LLMs and agentic AI, and an interest in where AI meets offensive security.
Exposure to detection and blue-team perspectives — knowing how your activity looks from the defender's side.
Infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Ansible) for repeatable target deployment.
What We Offer
100% Full-Remote, Flexible Part-Time (within Europe): ~20h/week, organized around your own schedule.
Expert Mentorship: Daily collaboration with top-tier industry experts in AI and Cyber Operations.
A Rare Vantage Point: Very few offensive security professionals get to shape an autonomous attacker from the inside. You'll be doing offensive work and defining what the next generation of it looks like.
Deep Tech Impact: Direct involvement in a Deep Tech project within the Defence and Security sector, with tangible impact on our technology roadmap.
Career Growth: Concrete path toward consolidation of the position and evolution into key operational roles as we scale.
How to Apply
Apply with your CV. If you have public offensive security work — CTF placements, write-ups, bug bounty credits, lab certifications — do make sure it's visible on your CV or LinkedIn, since that's what we'll be looking at most closely.

Job Description:
Job Description

About SkyGeo 

Everyday we provide our clients with essential geotechnical insights that allow them to understand very early how ground movement will impact their valuable assets. We have built an excellent and diverse team to approach InSAR increasingly as a professional service. To keep getting better at providing these insights at scale, we need the best people working with us. We are looking for colleagues who want to help build the business and to grow professionally by discovering a wide range of applications.

Your Role & Impact 

We have a position available for a Full-Stack Developer and Users Systems Architect to join our small, collaborative team, where we value individual freedom, responsibility, and each other.

In this role, you will:

Design, develop, and maintain a highly user-centric web application for SkyGeo's customers and internal stakeholders. 
Integrate SkyGeo's displacement mapping platform, subscription services, customer reports, invoicing, and administrative workflows into a centralized user management hub. 
Collaborate closely with stakeholders to gather user requirements and ensure the platform aligns with their needs. 
Designing APIs to support innovative geospatial insights products. 
Architect scalable solutions to handle growing user bases and data loads. 
Automate data delivery processes in the form of datasets, viewers, dashboards, and reports to customers. 
Support internal and external users with issues related to the platform. 
Set up and maintain CI/CD pipelines and manage resources in Amazon Web Services (AWS). 
Contribute to and execute against the product roadmap. 

Job Requirements

Ideal candidate 

Proven experience writing high-quality, maintainable production code in Python (particularly web frameworks such as Django and FastAP). 
Proficiency in JavaScript, Typescript, HTML, and CSS for creating user-centric interfaces (including frontend tools such as React and HTMX). 
Expertise in designing REST APIs, caching strategies, application monitoring, performance optimization, and handling request scaling in high-traffic environments. 
Strong experience in database management, SQL, ORMs and database migrations in a production environment (knowledge of PostgreSQL & PostGIS for geospatial data is advantageous). 
Proven track record of delivering high-quality, well-documented production software, including (unit)testing and refactoring. 
Experience working in Linux environment and managing Linux web servers. 
Working knowledge of modern DevOps tools and services, for example, Git, Gitlab CI/CD, Docker, AWS EC2 or K8S/AWS ECS/AWS Fargate. 
A strong affinity with containerization (Docker) and cloud technologies (AWS). 
Initiative to improve existing solutions and a collaborative approach to problem-solving. 
Attention to detail and a responsible attitude when working with sensitive data. 
Experience working with user management systems is a plus. 
Exposure to product ownership role is a plus. 

What’s In It For You

The opportunity to bring your experience, technical skills, and vision to help build next-generation Earth Observation applications and business 
A scale-up environment offering freedom, personal growth, and career development opportunities 
Diverse international team (10+ nationalities) 
Hybrid working environment (with an office in the historic city centre of Delft) 

A note on applying for multiple roles

We appreciate your interest in SkyGeo. If you see several vacancies that feel relevant to your background, we kindly ask you to apply for the role that best matches your skills, experience, and ambitions. At SkyGeo, we always look beyond just the vacancy or the resume. Our recruitment team carefully reviews each application and considers where your profile could make the strongest match within the company. If we see a better fit for another role, we will discuss this with you during the process. This helps us keep the application process clear, personal, and focused — for you and for us.
